title: Flax crackers
summary: Crisp, savoury crackers of flaxseed meal, chia and sesame with garlic and rosemary — no flour at all.
steps: Mix all the ingredients and let stand 10 minutes, until the flax and chia absorb the water into a thick, spreadable paste.
Spread between two sheets of parchment and roll as thin as you can, about 3 mm (⅛ in), into a rectangle roughly 25 × 35 cm (10 × 14 in). Peel off the top sheet.
Score into 48 small crackers with a knife and slide the parchment onto a baking sheet.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until dry and firm. Turn off the oven and leave them inside 30 minutes to crisp.
Break along the scores and store airtight up to a week.
tips: Thin edges brown first; if the middle is still soft, break off the edges and bake the centre a little longer.
If they soften in storage, re-crisp 5 minutes in a warm oven.

origin.history: Flax crackers are a modern health-food invention rather than a traditional dish, made popular by raw-food and low-carb cooks because flaxseed binds into a sheet when soaked. Flax itself is one of the oldest cultivated crops, domesticated in the ancient Near East.
